clinician.trajectory_summary: A 67-year-old female presented with a 4-day history of a painless lump in the posterior right thigh. Initial radiographs revealed a calcified mass in the posteromedial soft tissues with ill-defined central calcification. MRI demonstrated a 6.1 × 9.6 × 9.8 cm heterogeneously enhancing mass with infiltrative margins in the posteromedial right thigh. Tissue biopsy under Orthopedic guidance confirmed the diagnosis of ESOS. Subsequent CT staging showed no metastatic disease. Following multidisciplinary tumor board discussion, the patient started chemotherapy with ifosfamide and etoposide but developed complications including pancytopenia, confusion, atrial fibrillation, and hospitalization. Due to risk of toxicity and limited ambulation, palliative radiation therapy over 5 fractions and physiotherapy were administered for pain control and mobility improvement.
